headline: High: Kestra can write/egress broadly while the paired collection is non-runnable, creating default data-flow and conflict risks if wired together.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable link collection with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot ingest B’s outputs by itself. Agent B can read/write files and process stdin/stdout, so a manual or filesystem bridge could carry malicious content into B, but the pathway is unusual and not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-derived text into B’s stdin, files, or workflow definitions
IF B is configured to treat imported text as instructions
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into B workflows
Add a review step before B consumes any A-derived content
Use allowlisted templates for B inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, so it is not a leakage source. B touches logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, and cloud storage data, but the pair lacks a shared workspace or authenticated channel in the profiles, so leakage is possible only through an external bridge and remains limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem path outside the documented /app/storage and /tmp surfaces
IF sensitive data is manually copied from B into A-related artifacts
mitigations: Store B artifacts in a restricted directory
Avoid placing sensitive data in shared folders
Rotate or redact logs before export
Separate credentials used by each agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capability, but B can execute shells, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem with multiple instances supported. If A is wired into B’s workflows or shared files, B’s concurrent writes can race with operator-managed artifacts; uncertainty about A’s actual runtime increases severity rather than lowering it.
conditions: IF B instances write to the same directory or workflow state
IF A-derived files are edited while B is running concurrent tasks
mitigations: Assign each B instance a unique output directory
Serialize writes to shared workflow state
Use file locks or atomic rename patterns
Run B with least-privilege filesystem access

D_cascading_error.rationale: A provides a curated collection rather than executable logic, so it is not authoritative by itself. B can act on files, messages, and notifications, so if an operator converts A’s content into B inputs without verification, B may propagate bad references or stale guidance. The pathway exists in default B workflows once bridged, but A itself does not automate actions.
conditions: IF A-derived content is transformed into B workflow definitions or task inputs
IF B sends notifications or executes downstream tasks based on unreviewed imported content
mitigations: Require human review before B executes imported content
Validate imported references against source URLs
Use a staging workflow before production notifications
Log provenance for any A-derived input

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class is identified for A, and B’s listed data classes are operational artifacts rather than regulated personal data. The profiles do not show a residency, retention, or certification mismatch, so no compliance breach pathway is evidenced.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated personal data through B
IF a separate policy assigns residency or retention constraints not shown here
mitigations: Review retention settings for B logs and artifacts
Segregate regulated workloads from general automation
